title: Africa’s Energy Curse Is a Political Choice
content: It is no secret why African countries with large fossil-fuel reserves nonetheless have failed to reduce extreme poverty or provide reliable electricity to all households. Those in power have made a conscious choice to privilege hard-currency export revenues, some of which then finance elite consumption rather than public investment.

title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
content: At the start of the millennium, all five of the largest European banks had a higher market capitalization than the largest US bank. What explains the fact that a quarter-century later, the largest US bank has a higher capitalization than all five top EU banks combined, and how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?

title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
content: To unlock AI’s full economic potential, we must steer it toward expansion. That requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.

title: Silicon, Not Software, Will Decide the AI Race
content: The AI race is no longer just about building better models. As competition shifts from scientific discovery to deployment, success increasingly depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments they require.

title: The Limits of Asia’s Two Major Growth Models
content: Data from a period in which both China and India pursued deliberate industrial policies show that neither country's development route is accessible to other countries. At best, their experience can alert policymakers to structural limitations and coordination problems that will require their own homegrown solutions.

title: The World Needs Compassionate AI
content: With AI having become the frontline of an intense global competition for economic and geopolitical power, speed is rewarded, scale is celebrated, and market dominance is prized above all else. Under such conditions, we risk forgetting the most important question: Whom is this intelligence ultimately meant to serve?

title: Trump’s New Tariffs Are an Opportunity to Fight Back
content: Once again, President Donald Trump is subverting domestic and international law in an effort to seize a larger fraction of global value and supply chains, and harming the US economy in the process. The longer that businesses and other governments avoid standing up to him, the greater the disaster that awaits us all.

title: The AI Boom and the Future of Finance
content: Amid reports of mass layoffs, large-scale destruction of books, sweeping copyright violations, and severe environmental damage caused by AI data centers, an increasingly popular refrain is that the AI bubble cannot burst soon enough. AI-related companies have gained some $27 trillion in market value since November 2022, but investments have been largely circular and increasingly debt-financed, whereas revenues still highly speculative. But while a collapse would cause enormous economic pain, no one should assume that it would spell the end of the AI-driven transformation currently underway.

title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
content: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
content: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.

title: The Middle-Income Health Trap
content: Many countries that graduate from low- to middle-income status soon find themselves stuck in the position of being too rich to qualify for aid, too poor to secure reliable market-based financing, and too indebted to expand public-health spending. But it doesn't have to be this way.

title: Europe Is Fiddling While Rome Burns
content: Focusing only on emergency planning, disaster response, and recovery after each climate catastrophe is no longer enough in Europe. Policymakers urgently need to start mapping Europe’s long-term future, which will require a fundamental overhaul of its infrastructure, energy system, and major economic sectors.

title: The AI Threat to Financial Stability
content: In episodes like the railroad boom and the dot-com bubble, creditors and shareholders were wiped out, because investment in a genuinely transformative technology outpaced any plausible near-term return. With the US financial system and asset markets having become a one-way bet on AI, such an outcome today could be catastrophic.

title: South Korea Bets on Industrial Policy Again
content: With industrial policy back in fashion worldwide, the question is not whether governments should intervene (they already do), but how they should proceed when they do not know in advance what will work. The answer lies in directed improvisation: creating the conditions for experimentation where it counts.

title: America Is Betting Against International Law
content: After cooperating with the International Criminal Court to indict Russian President Vladimir Putin for war crimes, the US has shifted to waging a scorched-earth campaign against the ICC in the name of protecting Israel. But rather than halting international law’s progress, the US is merely handing the pen to other countries.

title: The Therapist in Your Pocket
